kinds.a: oil perfume · roll-on perfume oil · concentrated perfume oil (CPO)
kinds.d: Fragrance in an oil base with no alcohol, applied to the skin by roller or dab-on stick.
t: oil version of a fine fragrance

kinds.d: Natural distillate of flowers, herbs, earth or spices captured in a sandalwood or paraffin base by deg-bhapka distillation, then aged.

x.a: gulab attar · ruh gulab · attar of roses
x.d: Damask rose petals distilled into sandalwood oil; the classic Kannauj rose attar, a cooling summer scent.
x.dt: base: sandalwood or paraffin · ageing months to years · distillation repeated with fresh petals for strength

x.d: Baked clay distilled into sandalwood oil to capture the smell of first rain on dry earth; made in Kannauj.
x.dt: clay: kiln-baked discs or broken pots · distillation repeated over 10 days or more · stored in camel-skin flasks

x.d: Kannauj blend of 40 or more flowers, herbs and resins distilled together and aged for months; sweet, spicy and smoky.
Vetiver root oil, prized when distilled from wild north-Indian vetiver; a cooling summer attar.
x.dt: wild vs cultivated root · cool attar

x.d: Kewra flower distillate, one of the cool summer attars of Kannauj.
Jasmine-flower distillates, among the cool summer attars.
Saffron attar, one of the warm winter attars alongside musk and amber.

kinds.a: dehn al oud · dahn al oudh · agarwood oil · oudh oil
kinds.d: Oil distilled from resin-infected agarwood (Aquilaria), worn neat; scent varies with species, origin, wood part and distillation.

x.d: Agarwood oil from Assam and north-east India, known for strong, often barnyard-like profiles shaped by soaking and pot distillation.

v.n: Assam, Nagaland, Manipur and Meghalaya oils

x.dt: region: Upper Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Bhutan · fruity to barnyard · Aquilaria khasiana / malaccensis

x.d: Agarwood oil from Aquilaria crassna of Cambodia and neighbouring Indochina; often suggested as a gentler start than Hindi oils.
x.dt: Aquilaria crassna · Cambodia, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam

x.d: Agarwood oil from Aquilaria malaccensis and related species of Malaysia and Indonesia, including plantation wood.
x.dt: A. malaccensis, A. microcarpa, A. beccariana · wild vs plantation

kinds.a: rose otto · attar of roses · ward taifi
kinds.d: Rose essential oil worn as perfume, mostly from Rosa damascena, sold by region of origin.

x.d: Rose oil distilled in copper pots in the Taif mountains of Saudi Arabia each spring and sold by the tola.
x.dt: about 70,000 roses per tola · April harvest · oil vs rose water

x.d: Steam-distilled damask rose oil from the Rose Valley near Kazanlak.
Damask rose otto and absolute produced in Turkey.

kinds.d: Oil perfume built on musk, today almost always synthetic white musk; natural deer musk is CITES-controlled.

x.d: Clean white musk named for purity, used after bathing and in ritual purification; sold as oil, powder or stone.
x.dt: form: oil, powder, stone · used for body, clothing and linen

x.d: Musk from the gland of the male musk deer; trade is CITES-controlled and most offers are synthetic substitutes.

kinds.d: Arabian blended perfume oil combining oud, rose, amber, saffron, musk or woods into one dense accord.

brands.d: Family perfume house founded by Haji Ajmal Ali in Assam from the agarwood trade, now based in Dubai.
Saudi house rooted in a family oud-processing business of 1852, known for pure oud oils and Taif rose oils.
eras: Al Sheikh Abdul Samad Al Qurashi, from 1932

brands.d: Founded by Yemeni perfumer Hussein Adam Ali, the first Western-style Arabian perfume label in the UAE.
Bahraini house begun in Manama Souq by Asghar Ali, selling attars, concentrated oils and dehn al oudh.

traditions.d: Hydro-distillation of flowers, herbs and baked earth into a sandalwood base in copper stills; Kannauj perfumes hold a GI tag (2014).
traditions.tech: deg (copper still) sealed with clay, bamboo pipe to a bhapka of sandalwood oil, wood and cow-dung fire, repeated charges
traditions.mat: damask rose, jasmine, vetiver, kewra, baked clay, spices; sandalwood oil or liquid paraffin
traditions.auth: Kannauj GI tag; sandalwood rather than paraffin base; no alcohol; maker's distillery named

traditions.d: Wearing of dehn al oud, Taif rose oil, musk and blended mukhallat oils, traded by family houses in Gulf souqs.
traditions.tech: agarwood oil distillation; copper-pot distillation of Taif rose sold by the tola; blending into mukhallat
traditions.mat: agarwood (Aquilaria), Taif damask rose, white musk, amber, saffron
traditions.auth: origin and wood species stated; wild vs cultivated agarwood; natural oud oil yields are tiny, so cheap 'pure' oils are suspect

notes: Old k3 Perfume oil redistributed: Dehnal Oud Cambodi -> Cambodi oud oil version; Musk Tahara -> Musk tahara version; Warda Taif -> Taif rose oil version; Egyptian Musk kept as a musk-oil model. Dropped as shop-only blend SKUs: Ajwad, Amber Oud Attar, Damascus Rose (Attar Emporium); Romance, Sakeena, Sandal Rose, Sonia, White Oudh (Attar Mist). Maker 'Asghar Ali' normalised to Asgharali.
